_doc: ⚑ S401 (UiB job 29 D3; his 16 Nov, B11: "I think it would work beautifully when we arrive at the desk of Daniel at the end, and we see that text and the space transforms to the close") · ⚑ S404 (UiB job 30 C3; his 18 Nov: "I would say CRT, but the design of the Text should be more aesthetical"; "can we have a message for each stotyr line in diferent styles of the time shown on the CRT? in a way of dialoging with all the story lines"; on the third draft, "YES, this is much much better!"). At the end of 2026 the crossing lands at Daniel's desk; before the room becomes the Close, his monitor (the CRT that stands in the Close's row as his machine, S380) is on the desk again, dark, and on it four lines appear one after another, each in its own time's look, taken from the piece's own surfaces (src/room/danielLine.ts): a small 2016 over Vera's phone Notes and her newest note (data/dialog/s3_maiden.json notes `refusal`); a small 2026 over Maya's own message box, the line in it marked not sent (data/dialog/s4_v3.json bot.unsent); a small 2003 over the Messenger's window and Daniel's bubble (data/dialog/s2_caleb.json residue `line`, his ⟨S⟩ wording, VERBATIM, on one row, the type sized to fit, never re-wrapped); then, with no year, Caleb's answer in the same window (residue `answer`), a little larger, held longest. No names. Plain: no sound, no Lamby. The monitor is brought before the eye in every mode (heldDevice's grammar; the headset never turns, never fades), held while the lines are read and set back on the desk; then the transformation takes the room as before (the eyes rise, the stars, the cards, the panels). `?close=1` shows it too. The lines live where they are met; here: the years (display text) and the staging.
_docS404: ⚑ S404 — what job 29 D3 had here, kept: "answerAfter": 1.8, "holdExtra": 2.5 (`_docHold`: "the residue's `holdSeconds` (6.5) was for one line held alone in 2003; here two lines (16 words) are read, so the hold after Caleb's answer is holdSeconds + holdExtra"). D3's glass showed his line and Caleb's answer, plain white and silver on black in the 1997 face, under the Messenger's own lowercase nicks (`window.you` "daniel", `window.contact` "caleb"); the nicks are gone (his 5: no names). Now: `cards` one per line in order (Vera, Maya, Daniel, Caleb) with the small year above each of the first three; `cardAt` seconds after the monitor begins to lift (about 2 s apart); `reveal` how long the tube takes to draw a card in, top to bottom (no fade); `holdLast` how long Caleb's answer is held after it lands — dark 0.8 s + 7.4 s + 5 s ≈ 13 s on the glass, then 1.6 s back to the desk. `xrDist` 0.7 → 0.6: four lines, not two, are read in the headset. `glassMinPx` / `glassFill`: on a small view (a phone) the monitor comes closer, until its glass is that many CSS pixels wide or fills that much of the view.
